title: Coherent microlens motion led to smaller quasar disk estimates in simulations
summary: Ridge models trained on light curves that omitted relative microlens motion underestimated accretion-disk half-light radii by about 6% to 28% when tested on more detailed simulations. The comparison covered three quadruply lensed quasar configurations and used information from all four images jointly.
ai_technology: Ridge regression of simulated light-curve statistics
organization: Stony Brook University; City University of New York; American Museum of Natural History; University of Toronto; Université de Montréal; Mila

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§III, IV.2, IV.4 Table 2 and V.3

evidence.tested: Joint fits for three quadruply lensed quasar configurations and populations of 128 matched quads underestimated radii by 27.8%, 20.9% and 5.6% when training omitted relative motions. Matched-physics controls showed median biases between −0.003 and −0.001 dex.
evidence.unknown: The experiment simulated three fixed lens and disk configurations. It omitted survey selection, photometric noise, observing gaps and intrinsic variability, so the offsets are not corrections established for observed quasars.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted ridge regression maps simulated multiband light-curve statistics to logarithmic half-light radii. Models trained under simplified assumptions were applied to a separately partitioned target with independent lens motions and a lens mass distribution.
